title: Weak-coupling tensor cross interpolation impurity solver for nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory
authors: Shuta Matsuura, Hiroshi Shinaoka, Philipp Werner, Naoto Tsuji
abstract: Simulating nonequilibrium quantum many-body systems remains a major challenge due to the exponential growth of the computational complexity with real time. Here we implement a nonequilibrium impurity solver based on the weak-coupling expansion and the tensor cross interpolation (TCI), and apply it to nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT). The method approximates the integrands of the high-dimensional integrals arising in the weak-coupling expansion in a tensor-train form, enabling efficient evaluations without stochastic sampling and thereby mitigating the sign problem affecting continuous-time quantum Monte Carlo (CT-QMC) methods. Benchmark calculations for an exactly solvable nonequilibrium impurity model agree well with the exact results and reveal a low-rank structure of the integrands. When applied to interaction-quench problems in the half-filled Hubbard model, the method reproduces fast thermalization at a critical interaction strength with accuracy comparable to CT-QMC. Away from half filling, where the sign problem becomes even more severe, the present approach remains well controlled, revealing a crossover instead of a sharply defined fast thermalization point in the 3/4-filled case. The solver can also be applied to steady-state DMFT problems, yielding accurate spectral functions in the metallic regime without analytic continuation.
summary: The paper introduces an advanced impurity solver for nonequilibrium Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (DMFT) by combining weak-coupling expansion with Tensor Cross Interpolation (TCI). This technique efficiently calculates complex high-dimensional integrals, allowing accurate simulation of time evolution in strongly correlated electron systems like the Hubbard model. It is particularly valuable because it remains numerically controlled away from half-filling where other methods fail.
main_problem: Simulating nonequilibrium quantum many-body systems where computational complexity grows exponentially with real time.
main_result: The developed solver accurately reproduces known quench dynamics, showing that the dynamical transition at half-filling evolves into a smooth crossover when doping occurs.
method: It implements an impurity solver for Nonequilibrium Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (DMFT) using a weak-coupling expansion combined with the Tensor Cross Interpolation (TCI) algorithm to handle high-dimensional integrals efficiently.
model_or_system: The method is applied to lattice models, specifically the Hubbard model, analyzed via its mapping onto an impurity problem solved on the Keldysh contour in the complex time plane. The Hamiltonian involves interaction terms U(t).
key_observables: Two-time Green's functions (lesser/greater), spectral functions ($	ext{Im} G^R_\sigma(\omega)$), and quench dynamics.
important_parameters: Interaction strength U, filling fraction (e.g., half-filled vs 3/4-filled), maximum real time $t_{	ext{max}}$, and expansion order $n_{	ext{max}}$.
main_assumptions: The method relies on the weak-coupling expansion and assumes that the integrands possess a low-rank structure amenable to tensor decomposition via TCI.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate convergence checks showing error reduction with increasing expansion order ($n_{	ext{max}}$) or bond dimension ($\chi$), and compare TCI results against exact solutions for Green's functions in both time and frequency domains.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the mathematical framework by defining the Kadanoff-Baym contour, detailing iterative procedures for transient vs. steady states, and finally presenting the weak-coupling expansion solved via TCI to evaluate high-dimensional integrals.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful numerical tool that extends DMFT calculations into non-equilibrium regimes where standard Monte Carlo methods fail due to the sign problem, offering insights into real-time quantum dynamics.
